summary: This bill directs the Attorney General to develop or identify training curricula for command-level law enforcement personnel on leadership, incident response, risk management, officer wellness, data analysis, evidence-based decision making, and community trust-building, and to certify programs that incorporate these curricula.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to improve the COPS program by developing and certifying training curricula for command-level police personnel. This implies an increase in federal spending to fund the development, identification, and certification of these training programs, as well as the associated reporting requirements.

The core purpose of this bill is to enhance the training and effectiveness of command-level law enforcement personnel, focusing on leadership, critical incident response, risk management, officer wellness, data-driven policing, and building community trust. This directly aims to improve policing and criminal justice operations.
